How it works

Prep that feels practical, not theoretical every day counts!

Most learners don't fail IELTS from lack of English — they lose bands to timing, question traps and unpractised formats. TutorMigo trains the test itself, in small daily pieces.

  • ✓Timed drills that mirror the real clock — including Listening's single play
  • ✓Every wrong answer lands in your Mistake Notebook with the reason why
  • ✓Weekly mock scores feed your predicted band and re-balance your plan

Vocabulary for Band 7+

Topic word banks — environment, education, health, technology — with collocations, not single words.

132 / 300 words
  • sustainable — able to continue without harming the environment
  • allocate resources — to distribute money or time for a purpose
  • curriculum — the subjects taught in a school or course
  • sedentary lifestyle — a way of living with little physical activity
  • breakthrough — an important discovery or achievement
  • urbanisation — the growth of cities as people move into them
  • feasible — possible and practical to achieve
  • detrimental effect — a harmful impact on something
  • automation — using machines to do work previously done by people
  • well-being — the state of being comfortable, healthy and happy

Grammar Range Drills

Conditionals, passive voice and complex sentences — the range examiners reward in Writing & Speaking.

Reading · Set 15 · Speed sprint

Vertical Farming in the City

Read the passage, then answer 5 questions. Use the sprint timer to practise working at exam pace — one passage should take about 20 minutes in the real test.

10:00Sprint timer · 10 minutes

The passage

In warehouses and high-rise buildings near city centres, a new kind of farm is growing — upwards. Vertical farms stack layers of crops on top of one another under LED lights, allowing food to be produced in the middle of a city rather than hundreds of kilometres away.

The most frequently quoted advantage is water. Because water in a vertical farm is recycled in a closed loop, these farms can use up to 95 percent less water than conventional field farming. Supporters also point to yield: a well-run vertical farm can produce up to 350 times more food per square metre than a traditional farm growing the same crop.

Critics, however, focus on energy. Growing plants under artificial light is expensive, and a 2023 study in the Netherlands found that electricity accounted for around 40 percent of a vertical farm's running costs. Whether the model becomes mainstream, researchers argue, depends largely on how quickly renewable energy becomes cheaper.

Question 1 · True / False / Not Given

Vertical farms recycle the water they use.

Question 2 · True / False / Not Given

In the Dutch study, electricity made up about 40 percent of running costs.

Question 3 · True / False / Not Given

Most consumers prefer the taste of vertically farmed lettuce.

Question 4 · Multiple choice

A vertical farm can produce up to how much more food per square metre than a traditional farm?

Question 5 · Multiple choice

What is the critics' main concern about vertical farming?

      Task 1 warm-up

      Speaking · Parts 1–3

      Part 2 cue card, timed

      The full Speaking test lasts 11–14 minutes. Use the timers below to rehearse the exact rhythm: 1 minute to prepare, then speak for up to 2 minutes.

      Describe a skill you learned as a child

      You should say:

      • what the skill is
      • who taught you it, or how you learned it
      • how long it took you to learn
      • and explain why this skill is useful to you now
      1:00Preparation time · 1 minute
      Model answer (opening): "A skill I picked up when I was about nine is swimming, which my grandfather taught me at our local pool. At first I was terrified of the deep end, but he broke it down into tiny steps — floating, then kicking, then breathing properly. It took me roughly one summer to swim a full length without stopping. These days it's my main form of exercise, and honestly it's also how I switch off after a stressful day of studying…"

      Part 1 · warm-up questions

      • Do you work, or are you a student?
      • What do you enjoy most about your studies?
      • How do you usually spend your weekends?

      Part 3 · discussion questions

      • Should schools teach more practical skills, such as cooking or managing money?
      • Is it easier for children to learn new skills than for adults? Why?
      • How might technology change the skills people need in the future?

      Study Plan

      Your 4 weeks to exam day

      Built backwards from your exam date and your weakest section. Tap a task to mark it done — Writing gets extra weight until it reaches 7.0.

      Week 1: 0 of 9 tasks done

      Mon · Listening

      Parts 1–2 basics

      • Set 19 — form completion (10 Q)
      • Spelling drill: names, dates, numbers
      • 10 vocabulary words — education
      Wed · Reading

      Skim & scan

      • Passage 1 timed — 20 minutes
      • True / False / Not Given clinic
      • Review 6 notebook mistakes
      Fri · Writing

      Task 1 structure

      • Bar chart overview paragraph x2
      • Paraphrasing practice — 5 prompts
      • Speaking Part 1 record — hometown
      Mon · Writing

      Task 2 deep work

      • Opinion essay — full 40 minutes
      • Band 7 model essay breakdown
      • Complex sentence drills x10
      Wed · Speaking

      Cue card fluency

      • 3 cue cards with partner
      • Part 3 linking phrases practice
      • 10 vocabulary words — technology
      Sat · Mixed

      Half mock

      • Listening full test — 40 questions
      • Reading Passage 2 + 3 timed
      • Log all mistakes in notebook
      Mon · Reading

      Speed week

      • Full Reading paper — strict 60 min
      • Matching headings strategy review
      • Speed sprint x2
      Wed · Listening

      Trap training

      • Part 3 multiple choice x3 sets
      • Map labelling practice
      • Distractor-spotting review
      Fri · Writing

      Both tasks, timed

      • Task 1 process diagram — 20 min
      • Task 2 discussion essay — 40 min
      • Self-check with band descriptors
      Mon · Mock 1

      Full simulation

      • Full mock — 2 hrs 40 min, one sitting
      • Speaking mock with partner
      • Error review — top 10 mistakes
      Wed · Mock 2

      Second simulation

      • Full mock under exam timing
      • Compare bands vs Mock 1
      • Light revision only in the evening
      Exam Eve

      Wind down

      • Skim vocabulary notebook — 20 min max
      • Prepare ID, pencils & test centre route
      • Sleep early — no new material

      Mistake Notebook

      Your errors, organised — so they stop repeating

      Every mistake from practice and mocks is saved here with its correction. Reveal the fix, then drill it until it disappears.

      mistakes are data, not failure

      Listening · Spelling × 9

      ✕ "accomodation" — written in Part 1 form completion

      Why it costs you: Listening answers are marked wrong for spelling, even when you heard the word correctly.

      ✓ accommodation — double c, double m. Added to your spelling drill list.

      Writing · Task Response × 6

      ✕ Opinion stated in the introduction, then changed in the conclusion

      Why it costs you: an unclear or shifting position caps Task Response — often the difference between Band 6 and 7.

      ✓ Pick one position, preview it in the intro, and restate the same position in the conclusion.

      Speaking · Fluency × 5

      ✕ Long pauses before Part 3 answers while searching for the "perfect" word

      Why it costs you: examiners reward flow. A simpler word said smoothly scores higher than a pause.

      ✓ Use a filler bridge — "Well, one way to look at it is…" — and keep talking while you think.
